jobs.jobDescription:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

Credit-based and consumption-based offerings are becoming central to how GitLab monetizes. The systems that meter, rate, and bill that consumption sit underneath all of it. You'll own the backend usage billing pipeline and its product direction while supporting the Monetization Platform and Infrastructure team as it modernizes the foundations underneath it.

When another GitLab team launches a credit-consuming capability, you'll help them make it billable across GitLab.com, self-managed, and GitLab Dedicated. This is a technical, systems-oriented product role: success means building a monetization platform other teams can launch on quickly and correctly, rather than shipping customer-facing UI.

What you’ll do

  • Own the product direction for metering, aggregation, and rating in GitLab's usage billing pipeline, including the Zuora and CustomersDot integrations that turn usage into invoiced revenue.
  • Make onboarding a new credit-consuming capability a repeatable process rather than a bespoke project each time.
  • Partner with product teams on what to instrument, how to meter and price usage across GitLab.com, self-managed, and GitLab Dedicated, and what it takes to be billable on launch day. Stay ahead of their roadmaps so billing doesn't delay launches.
  • Prioritize pipeline scalability, performance, and reliability as consumption grows, balancing those investments against new capability enablement.
  • Own billing defect detection and remediation so errors surface before they reach a customer's invoice and billing outcomes remain auditable.
  • Support the Monetization Platform and Infrastructure team by framing problems, explaining the value of platform investments, and prioritizing them against operational risk.
  • Define and track measures of billing accuracy, pipeline reliability, cost to serve per capability, and time to monetize so teams can make informed pricing decisions.

What you’ll bring

  • Experience owning the product direction of consumption- or usage-based billing systems.
  • Experience with Zuora or a comparable billing and revenue platform, and an understanding of how product and finance systems interact.
  • Experience with prepaid, commitment, or credit-drawdown pricing models (balances, reservations, overage, expiration) and the edge cases they create in billing and revenue.
  • Experience launching new products or pricing models while coordinating across engineering, Finance, Legal, Compliance and go-to-market teams.
  • Ability to bring together teams you don't manage around work their launches depend on.
  • Experience defining problems for platform or backend teams whose users are often other teams.
  • Clear written communication in an all-remote, asynchronous environment; you'll use issues, epics, and direction pages to lead.
  • Familiarity with developer tooling, financial audit or revenue recognition, or an engineering background can help, but isn't required.
  • You use AI tools as part of how you work: prototyping, analysis, spec writing, and investigation.

About the team

In Monetization, we coordinate across engineering, Finance, Legal, Compliance and go-to-market on new products and pricing models. Our remote, asynchronous work uses written issues, and epics to keep decisions visible.

Remote-Global

Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. jobs.jobDescription:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We’re hiring a Product Manager to own the core ElevenCreative product experience for creators and marketers who sign up, subscribe, and build on their own. Self-serve users make up the majority of ElevenCreative’s user base, and they use the platform to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

You’ll drive growth and adoption across the self-serve product experience, focusing on how users discover what ElevenCreative can do, how they move from a first generation into agents, video, and multi-step creative workflows, and what keeps them coming back and upgrading. There’s no shortage of things we could build. The job is defining the big bets, scoping them well, and shipping them quickly with the team.

PMs at ElevenLabs work in small, highly collaborative teams with minimal process, alongside engineers who have room to build creatively and lead. The scope is broad by design. Some weeks lean toward product, others toward growth or go-to-market work, and you’ll own whatever it takes to make ElevenCreative the best product for its users.

What you’ll do

  • Drive growth and adoption of the self-serve product, focusing on onboarding, activation, and upgrade moments, and partnering with growth, lifecycle, and pricing teams where they connect

  • Scope and define the big bets for the self-serve product across image, video, music, agents, and editing workflows

  • Find the biggest opportunities in the user journey through product data and user behavior, and turn them into clearly scoped projects

  • Drive adoption of newer experiences like agents and video, helping users expand from a single product into the full platform

  • Work with engineering and design to ship quickly, mocking up early concepts yourself when it speeds things up

  • Partner with growth, lifecycle, and social teams on launches and the moments that bring users into new parts of the product

  • Define success metrics for your area and track activation, engagement, retention, and conversion to paid plans

  • Talk to creators and marketers regularly to understand how they work and where the product falls short, and bring those insights back to the team

Requirements

  • 5+ years of product management experience on consumer or self-serve products

  • A track record of moving growth and adoption metrics through the products you’ve shipped

  • Deep familiarity with the creative space and the creators and marketers who use these tools, with a habit of bringing user insights into every product decision

  • Experience scoping and defining large, ambiguous bets and owning them end to end

  • Design-minded, with a high bar for quality and user experience and the ability to mock up concepts yourself

  • Technical fluency to go deep with engineers on how things are built and the tradeoffs involved

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort in product analytics tools to find opportunities and measure impact

  • A track record of shipping quickly and iterating based on what the data shows

  • Ownership pedigree, meaning you drive your own projects fully rather than handing off after the spec

  • Curiosity about AI and creative tools, and close attention to how the space is moving

About Veriff

Veriff is building trust infrastructure for the internet. Our AI-powered identity verification and fraud prevention platform helps businesses across fintech, crypto, gaming, mobility and marketplaces know who their users are, and whether they can be trusted, in 230+ countries and territories. We build our own technology end to end, and every verification we run teaches us something about how fraud really works.

The role

Veriff sees fraud at a scale and breadth that no single platform can see on its own. Our job now is to turn that advantage into products customers can see, measure and act on, and to build the network that makes it compound.

As Lead Product Manager for Fraud on the Veriff Network team, you will make the fraud detection, prevention and accuracy strengths of our product legible to customers. You will own the concrete product experiences that do this, such as a Feedback API that lets customers tell us what happened after a decision, fraud insights inside Station (our customer portal), and automated fraud reporting. You will also lead the customer engagement that turns those experiences into a feedback loop: customers share outcomes and signals, our detection gets sharper, and every platform on the network benefits.

This is one of the first roles on the Veriff Network, and it directly shapes how we package, sell and grow our fraud offering.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days, you will have assessed our fraud product roadmap and packaging and agreed a revised version with product and fraud leadership. You will have identified the top three to five fraud product improvements, with the highest-priority items shaped and in development.

By six months, the first updated fraud product offering is live with a group of design and beta partners.

By nine to twelve months, a shared-signal pilot is running with a set of platforms, as the first step toward a cross-platform fraud network.

By twelve months, the improved fraud products are generally available and are measurably helping us attract and close deals with our core customer segments.

What you'll bring

  • Fraud and risk expertise. You have shipped fraud or risk products, or you have been responsible for fighting fraud and managing risk at a scaled, digital-native company. You understand attack patterns, how fraud teams actually work day to day, and how the precision/recall trade-off plays out in the real world.
  • Network product experience. You have worked on network-effect or marketplace data products, where aligning incentives between participants and building feedback loops are central to the product.
  • Data and ML product craft. You can specify a signal, read a model evaluation, and ship and manage a rules engine. You know what to build yourself and what to leave to data science.
  • Customer discovery with fraud teams. You can get fraud and trust leaders at platforms talking openly, and you turn what you learn into a clear roadmap.

Nice to have

  • Experience building with operations teams. Our fraud operations experts are the source of truth on what fraud looks like in practice, and the right person turns their judgment into product. If you haven't worked closely with an operations team before, you'll need to show strong cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Commercial packaging. You have shaped how a product is priced and sold, and worked deals alongside Sales.

Why Veriff?

We are the preferred identity verification platform partner for the world’s most innovative growth-driven organizations helping conveniently verify and safeguard users anywhere in the world. We support the broadest number of identity documents from nearly every country and territory in the world - and this is continually increasing! With a diverse team in the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, and Estonia, as well as robust backing and funding from investors including Accel, Alkeon, IVP, Tiger Capital, and Y Combinator, we’re dedicated to helping businesses and individuals build a safer and more secure world. We strive to be the benchmark for trust online, and we take pride in being a positive force.When you join Team Veriff, we offer you the opportunity to have a real impact and advance your career whilst looking after you along the way with a range of benefits designed with you in mind. Some of our favourites include...

  • Flexibility to work from home
  • Stock options that ensure your share in our success
  • Extra recharge days on top of your annual vacation
  • Extensive medical, dental, and vision insurance to ensure you’re feeling great physically and mentally
  • Learning and Development & Health and Sports budget that you are free to tailor to your own needs
  • Four weeks of fully paid sabbatical leave after reaching your 5th work anniversary

We are an Equal Opportunities employer committed to a diverse and representative team. Different opinions, perspectives, and personalities push us forward. We want to hear from people who are passionate about their work and align with our values. Regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability. We also know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting spectacular candidates - so rest assured, whoever you are, we want to hear from you!

Please take the time to read our Recruitment Privacy Notice, which explains how we collect and process your data for recruitment-related activities in accordance with applicable laws. Please read the information carefully. By submitting the application with the required information, you acknowledge that Veriff processes the information for recruitment purposes. Please be informed that in the final stage of the recruitment process, we may request that you undergo identity verification. For more information, please see Recruitment Privacy Notice. #US1#SPBTAL #LI-Remote

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

The Site Selection & Colocation Manager is responsible for identifying, evaluating, and securing optimal locations for new data center developments and colocation expansions. This role combines real estate strategy, technical due diligence, market analysis, and vendor management to support the company’s global data center growth. The manager will collaborate closely with engineering, construction, finance, legal, and network planning teams to ensure that selected sites meet operational, technical, and business requirements.

You’re welcome to work in our office in Amsterdam or Remote in the EU.

Your responsibilities will include:

Site Selection & Market Analysis

  • Lead the end-to-end site selection process for new data center facilities.
  • Conduct market assessments, including power availability, fiber connectivity, land suitability, regulatory requirements, and risk factors.
  • Build and maintain market intelligence on emerging data center regions, supply trends, energy markets, and colocation pricing.
  • Evaluate and shortlist candidate sites through comparative analysis, scoring models, and feasibility studies.

Technical & Environmental Due Diligence

  • Coordinate environmental, geotechnical, hydrological, and seismic assessments.
  • Assess infrastructure availability (power, water, fiber) and future scalability.
  • Evaluate construction constraints, climate conditions, logistics access, and permitting feasibility.
  • Work with engineering teams to ensure sites meet mechanical, electrical, and network resilience requirements.

Colocation Strategy & Vendor Management

  • Identify colocation providers and evaluate facilities based on technical specifications, SLA requirements, and cost structure.
  • Lead RFPs, negotiations, and contract execution with colocation and connectivity partners.
  • Manage colocation lifecycle: renewals, expansions, migrations, and optimization of space/power allocations.
  • Monitor vendor performance against SLA, uptime, compliance, and efficiency metrics.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work with data center design and construction teams to validate site feasibility and development timelines.
  • Partner with legal on contract terms, property acquisition, lease terms, and regulatory compliance.
  • Support finance with CapEx/OpEx modeling, ROI calculations, and business case development.
  • Coordinate with public authorities, utilities, and permitting agencies as needed.

Risk Assessment & Compliance

  • Evaluate risks related to natural hazards, geopolitical risk, security, environmental constraints, and utility reliability.
  • Ensure compliance with local regulations, zoning laws, and corporate standards.
  • Maintain documentation for audits, reporting, and internal approvals.

We expect you to have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Real Estate, Engineering, Business, Geography, or related field.
  • 5–8+ years of experience in site selection, real estate development, colocation management, or data center infrastructure.
  • Strong understanding of data center power, cooling, and network requirements.
  • Experience in evaluating colocation providers and negotiating leases/SLAs.
  • Analytical skills in market research, cost modeling, and risk assessment.
  • Ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects across regions.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience with hyperscale or large-scale data center development.
  • Knowledge of utility procurement (power, water), renewable energy markets, and substation planning.
  • Familiarity with geospatial tools (GIS), risk modeling, or data center capacity planning.
  • Understanding of permitting processes and environmental regulations.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

jobs.jobDescription:
Who We Are

Our mission is to make the world programmable. Sight is one of the key ways we understand the world, and soon this will be true for the software we use, too.

We’re building the tools, community, and resources needed to make the world programmable with artificial intelligence. Roboflow simplifies building and using computer vision models. Today, over 1M+ developers, including those from half the Fortune 100, use Roboflow’s machine learning open source and hosted tools. That includes counting cells to accelerate cancer research, improving construction site safety, digitizing floor plans, preserving coral reef populations, guiding drone flight, and much more.

Our team is small relative to our impact, and we believe our user success is our success (not the inverse). A team member summarized: “Roboflow is a company full of giant brains and tiny egos.” We find software has a multiplier effect on all roles (not only product and engineering), so Roboflow employs developers across the company in design, sales, customer support, marketing, and beyond.

We’re supported by great customers and investors, having raised over 63 million from Google Ventures, Y Combinator, Craft Ventures, Sam Altman, Lachy Groom, amongst other leading software investors.

What You'll Do

We’re hiring a Sales Operations Analyst to run the day-to-day operating rhythm of our revenue team and to stand up our deal desk, reporting into the Revenue Operations lead and working closely with sales leadership, finance, and our GTM Systems Engineer. Revenue Operations owns the operating system for go-to-market at Roboflow: how pipeline is measured, how the forecast is built, how territory and quota are set, and whether the numbers can be trusted. This role is the analytical and commercial half of that mandate. You’ll own the analysis leadership makes decisions from, and you’ll be the person reps come to when a deal needs to be structured, priced, and approved.

You’ll work alongside a GTM Systems Engineer who builds and maintains the systems themselves. Where they own how Salesforce works, you own what the numbers mean and how a deal gets done. Our motion is land-and-expand into enterprise manufacturing with packaged site licenses and a fast-growing first-land play, so deal structuring here is real work with real leverage, and the forecast has several distinct models underneath it.

  • Own day-to-day deal desk duties: guide reps on deal structure and packaging, run pricing and discount approvals, handle non-standard terms, and drive the path from quote to signed order form, including cloud marketplace transactions

  • Maintain pricing and packaging guardrails with Finance and sales leadership, including approval thresholds, discount bands, and the guidance reps use to size a site license or a proof of value

  • Contribute to the weekly and monthly forecast process: assemble the forecast, track submitted forecast against actuals, and surface slip, drift, and coverage gaps by segment

  • Own the recurring analysis leadership decides from, including pipeline generation, conversion by stage and segment, win/loss, sales cycle, and team performance

  • Support territory, coverage, and quota planning with account distribution, whitespace, capacity math, and attainment tracking

  • Steward KPI definitions so a number means the same thing in every meeting, dashboard, and report, and be the person who can explain any of them on the spot

  • Run the data quality cadence with reps: publish the cleanup views, work each list down with its owner, and escalate recurring problems for a systems fix

  • Support the variable compensation program through attainment reporting, plan mechanics, and the data quality behind both

Who You Are

You are a commercially minded analyst, equally comfortable in a spreadsheet and in the middle of a live deal, who wants to be an important part of an exceptional team that focuses on using Roboflow's computer vision tools to impact and improve every industry. You have high agency and a bias toward action.

Required Skills:

  • 3+ years in sales operations, revenue operations, deal desk, or a sales-facing analytics role at a B2B software company

  • Strong analytical skills: you can build and defend a model in a spreadsheet, and you write SQL or will pick it up quickly

  • Hands-on Salesforce experience as a power user, including reports, dashboards, pipeline inspection, and opportunity and forecast data

  • Practical understanding of GTM mechanics: pipeline stages, forecast categories, coverage, win rates, territory and quota concepts

  • Experience supporting deal structuring, pricing approvals, or quote-to-order workflows

  • A clear communicator who can explain a number to a skeptical audience and hold a definition under pressure

  • High attention to detail, because this role is the last check before a number reaches leadership or a customer

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience running or standing up a deal desk, particularly with packaged or tiered pricing

  • Experience with CPQ, quoting tools, CLMs, or e-signature platforms

  • SQL plus experience with a BI tool or data warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, or similar)

  • Experience with enterprise land-and-expand motions, PLG, or developer-first companies

  • Experience supporting variable compensation or quota administration

  • Experience using AI tools to speed up analysis, documentation, and reporting

Where You'll Work

Roboflow is a fully distributed company. We currently have Hubs in New York City, San Francisco and Brazil (and plan to open more as we grow density in new cities). We provide opportunities (like team onsites in different cities) and resources (like a $4000/yr travel stipend) to work in person with other team members as much as you'd like, while also supporting remote team members. You can work from one of our Hubs (we offer a relocation bonus), work from home, work at co-working spaces, etc. We want you to work where you work best!

What You'll Receive

To determine your salary, we use a number of market and data-driven salary sources. We review all salaries every six months to ensure we stay in line with the market.

In addition to our cash compensation, we offer generous perks and benefits. Below are some of the highlights:

  • $4000/yr Travel Stipend to travel anywhere anytime to work alongside other Roboflowers

  • Cover up to 100% of your health insurance costs for you and your partner or family

Below is the interview process you can expect for this role. We’re committed to building an exceptional team and aim to be thoughtful while also moving quickly. We respect your time and strive to make decisions efficiently, depending on scheduling and availability.

You’ll have several conversations with the hiring manager, a member of the Roboflow leadership team, and complete a role-relevant project or challenge.

Throughout the process, you’ll speak directly with team members about what it’s like to work and succeed at Roboflow. Below is the interview process you can expect for this role.

  • The best way to stand out is to write about something you’ve built with Roboflow or contribute to one of our open source projects.

Introduction Phase:

  • [30m] Meet with recruiter and/or hiring manager to assess for overall mindset and skillset

  • [45m] Technical Assessment, if applicable

Team Interview Phase:

  • [30m] Meet with another member of the team

  • [60m] Meet with hiring manager again

  • Use this time to review specifics about the job description

  • Begin working through your 30/60/90 projects

  • Ask questions!

Build with Roboflow Phase

  • You will build a small project with Roboflow to showcase your technical and product skills.

  • [45m] Meet with your hiring manager and our CTO, Brad Dwyer to demo your project

Final Interview Stage

  • [30m] Leadership conversation focused on culture and company vision, as applicable.

  • [30m] Additional leadership discussion to discuss culture, as applicable.

References

  • References are required as part of our process. We will reach out to coordinate timing.

Note: you are welcome to request additional conversations with anyone you would like to meet and we will accommodate as best we can.

Not sure if this is you?

We want a diverse, global team with a broad range of experience and perspectives. We carefully consider every application and will either move forward with you, find another team that might be a better fit, keep in touch for future opportunities, or thank you for your time.

We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About The Role

As Headway works to build a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access, we’re facing unique operational challenges and opportunities that come with growing and scaling at an unparalleled rate. We’re pushing the boundaries of the existing healthcare system so that we can fulfill our promise to providers, patients, and payers to create access to high quality providers across the nation. In order to do that, we’re building a world class operations team that enables efficiency, growth, and quality, and as a member of this team, you will have the opportunity to have a material impact on the trajectory of Headway and help define a function core to the livelihood of our business and the impact we deliver for our partners and clients.

As a Business Operations Manager, you will lead high-impact, cross-functional initiatives that span teams and pods. You’ll operate as a thought partner to Product, Data, and Operations leaders – helping shape objectives, influence priorities, and translate complex insights into actionable plans. In addition to owning critical operational workflows, you’ll design scalable systems, mentor team members, and drive initiatives that create durable, measurable impact across the organization. This role requires strong judgment, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to drive alignment and execution across the organization.

What you’ll do at Headway

  • Design and build foundations for a variety of 0-1 initiatives within the Business Operations function.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally to build, execute, monitor, and implement scalable products and processes that enable us to deliver on core business challenges.

  • Assess and analyze data to develop and determine strategies for accelerating progress, proactively identify areas for improvement, and deliver on roadmap priorities and team OKRs.

  • Build and manage a growing team to achieve these objectives.

You’ll be great for this role if you:

  • 7+ years of experience in operational roles at high-growth companies, with some background in consulting, finance, business operations preferred but not required.

  • Data is your first-language; you enjoy and are skilled at digging through complex data to solve ambiguous problems.

  • You thrive in the unknown, and seek out opportunities to dive into unfamiliar challenges, drive towards outcomes, and shape strategy.

  • You are operationally excellent, able to manage a large volume of moving pieces without breaking a sweat.

  • You are a collaborator that proactively partners across teams while holding teams accountable for business results.

  • You seek an environment that fosters individual growth through open-feedback and high-autonomy.

  • You are motivated by the opportunity to make an impact on one of our generation’s defining problems: affordable mental healthcare

Compensation:

The expected base pay range for this position is $121,600 - $190,000 based on a variety of factors including qualifications, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for an equity grant, depending on the position and level.

About the role:

You will be the first dedicated PM for pricing at Headway. Your mission: build pricing into a durable, experimentation-driven lever for growth and revenue. Success looks like creating $100M+ of revenue impact.

Headway's pricing decisions affect every participant in our marketplace — what providers earn, what patients pay, and what payers reimburse. Today, these decisions are made through a mix of analysis, intuition, and competitive benchmarks. You'll replace that with a systematic, experiment-driven approach that generates data, builds conviction, and creates new revenue streams through bundling/un-bundling.

This is not a strategy-deck role. You will design experiments, partner with data scientists, navigate cross-functional complexity, and ship pricing changes that move the business. You'll work at the intersection of product, economics, and marketplace dynamics in one of the fastest-growing healthcare companies in the country.

  • Own pricing experimentation end-to-end: Design, run, and analyze pricing experiments (payout levels, take rates, fee structures, incentive models) with proper controls and measurement.

  • Price and package existing features: Identify opportunities to unbundle, tier, or price Headway's existing feature set as new revenue lines, while balancing the provider experience.

  • Define Headway's pricing philosophy: Build a principled, defensible approach to how we set prices — transparent to providers, competitive in the market, and sustainable for the business.

  • Inform tiering with pricing data: Partner with other product teams to ensure pricing and tier design are grounded in experimental evidence, willingness-to-pay research, and elasticity data.

  • Build the experimentation infrastructure: Work with Engineering and Data to create systems that enable rapid, controlled pricing experiments across geographies and segments.

  • Navigate cross-functional complexity: Align Finance, Provider Growth, Payer, Ops, and Legal around pricing decisions that affect every part of the business.

Who You Are

  • 8+ years of PM experience, with at least 2-3 years owning pricing, monetization, or marketplace economics.

  • You've personally owned pricing or packaging strategy and shipped changes that moved revenue.

  • You've designed and run pricing experiments at scale — you know the difference between a feature A/B test and a pricing experiment.

  • Strong quantitative fluency — you can partner with data scientists on experiment design and causal inference as a peer.

  • You thrive in ambiguity and can build structure where none exists — this is a new team.

  • Bonus: SaaS pricing & packaging experience (PLG, tiering, bundling).

About Us

With electric vehicles expected to be nearly 30% of new vehicle sales by 2025 and more than 50% by 2040, electric mobility is becoming a reality. ChargePoint (NYSE: CHPT) is at the center of this revolution, powering one of the world’s leading EV charging networks and a comprehensive set of hardware, software and mobile solutions for every charging need across North America and Europe. We bring together drivers, businesses, automakers, policymakers, utilities and other stakeholders to make e-mobility a global reality.

Since our founding in 2007, ChargePoint has focused solely on making the transition to electric easy for businesses, fleets and drivers. ChargePoint offers a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to create an all-electric future and a trillion-dollar market.

At ChargePoint, we foster a positive and productive work environment by committing to live our values of Be Courageous, Charge Together, Love our Customers, Operate with Openness, and Relentlessly Pursue Awesome. These values guide how we show up every day, align, and work together to build a brighter future for all of us.

Join the team that is building the EV charging industry and make your mark on how people and goods will get everywhere they need to go, in any context, for generations to come.

Reports To

Senior Director, Data and Product Management

What You Will Be Doing

  • Own the product strategy, roadmap, and outcomes for ChargePoint's fleet software platforms — including ViriCiti (telematics and fleet management) and new platforms being developed for truck fleets and autonomous vehicle operators.
  • Drive the evolution of existing platforms: identify gaps in the current customer experience, prioritize improvements, and ensure the platform continues to meet the needs of today's fleet operators while scaling for future growth.
  • Define and build net-new software products for emerging fleet segments, including purpose-built solutions for commercial truck charging management and autonomous vehicle fleet operations.
  • Translate customer needs, market trends, and business priorities into clear product requirements, user stories, and success metrics — working closely with engineering and design to ship high-quality software.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams including sales, marketing, customer success, and data science to align on market opportunities, support go-to-market execution, and drive adoption of fleet software solutions.
  • Engage directly with fleet customers and prospects to deeply understand their workflows, pain points, and evolving software needs — bringing the voice of the customer into every product decision.
  • Communicate product vision, progress, and trade-offs clearly to a wide array of stakeholders, from engineering teams to executive leadership.

ChargePoint is seeking a Staff Product Manager, Fleet Software to own the software product strategy and roadmap for our fleet vertical. Reporting to the Senior Director, Product, you will be responsible for the full lifecycle of ChargePoint's fleet software platforms in North America and Europe — from maintaining and evolving our existing solutions such as ViriCiti to defining and building new platforms for emerging segments including truck and autonomous vehicle fleets. This is an individual contributor role in which you will operate as a hands-on product leader, partnering closely with engineering, design, data, and go-to-market teams to ship software that fleet operators love.

Requirements

  • 12 years of product management experience, with a strong focus on software products — ideally in fleet management, telematics, mobility, energy management, or adjacent SaaS platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage and evolve existing software platforms while simultaneously defining new products from the ground up.
  • Experience working with fleet operators, commercial vehicle customers, or logistics companies preferred
  • Strong technical fluency — able to engage meaningfully with engineering teams on software architecture, APIs, and data pipelines without needing to write code.
  • Customer-obsessed and data-driven, with experience translating qualitative customer insight and quantitative data into prioritized product decisions.
  • Intellectually curious, analytical, creative, collaborative, and a strategic thinker who can work effectively as an individual contributor in a matrixed organization.
  • Strong communication skills — able to translate complex technical and commercial concepts into clear, structured narratives for diverse stakeholders.
  • Based in North America

North America - Remote

The company offers a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance; 401(k); paid time off; parental leave; life and disability insurance; and wellness resources.

jobs.jobDescription:
GiveDirectly has delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty across 15 countries since 2011. We believe cash transfers are one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid, with the research to back it up. Our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026.

Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We support high ownership and real professional growth. Curious about what it's really like to work here? Read our values and hear from the people who do. If they resonate, this could be a great fit!

Reports to: Vice President, Partnerships

Level: Director (we are open to hiring at Senior Director level for more experienced candidates)

Role overview

GiveDirectly intends to transfer $10B by 2035 while building a resilient, durable cash-first movement in the aid sector.

To reach this milestone, we have brought all fundraising efforts under one leadership, to enable better coordination and optimisation of fundraising streams and operations over time. This unified approach is building a high-performance fundraising team that identifies and secures high-quality leads, while standardizing revenue operations and knowledge-sharing across all verticals, enabling a better donor experience and securing long-term funding to achieve our goals of eliminating extreme poverty and responding better in crisis.

The Director/Senior Director, Revenue Operations will own the operating backbone of the Fundraising function: the data, systems, and processes that let Partnerships, Philanthropy, Individual Giving, and Special Projects run at scale. As we grow our Emergency Cash and US work alongside our work on ending extreme poverty, the candidate will also help ensure fundraising strategies are complementary rather than competing. This is a BizOps-first role. You will build the pipeline infrastructure, KPI architecture, and operating rhythms that make Fundraising's growth predictable and measurable, and you will represent Fundraising to Finance, Compliance, Grants Management, and the People team.

Alongside this, the role carries a chief-of-staff dimension: partnering with the Vice President of Partnership on strategic priorities, high-stakes internal and external communications, and organizational change management, so the VP's time is focused on the highest-impact work.

Depending on the skills and interests of the person we hire, this role may grow to manage a team of 3-5, covering some combination of: fundraising tech and data (e.g. Salesforce), donor experience, and knowledge management. Reflecting our "Team Next" value and commitment to organizational excellence, this person will drive cross-functional collaboration to ensure fundraising operations scale seamlessly alongside our global growth.

Key responsibilities

Own Fundraising's revenue operations: data, systems, and process (primary focus)

  • Build and own the strategic data and systems architecture for Fundraising: pipeline tracking, annual and in-year forecasting, and reporting infrastructure (e.g. Salesforce) that gives every vertical a single, trustworthy source of truth.
  • Define, standardize, and own tracking of fit-for-purpose Fundraising KPIs, aligned to Board reporting needs and the team's long-term strategic direction.
  • Partner with counterparts on Fundraising Data and Tech to prioritize, execute, and approve projects that serve both functions.
  • Design and institutionalize the operating rhythms of the Fundraising function: pipeline reviews, QBRs, reporting cadences, and the processes that turn strategy into consistent execution.
  • Develop revenue systems and processes alongside the Finance, Fundraising and Donor Experience teams that support scalable growth, protect donor journeys, and ensure capital moves securely and efficiently through the organization.
  • Own revenue reconciliation and recognition, pledge and receivable tracking, restricted-fund coding, monthly/annual close handoff, or audit support.
  • Own workforce and capacity planning for Fundraising in partnership with the VP: role scoping, hiring prioritization, and structural improvements as the team scales.

Build and lead a team as the function matures

  • As the role grows, manage a team of 3-5 covering fundraising tech and data (e.g. Salesforce), donor experience, and knowledge management, setting priorities, coaching, and ensuring quality across each area.
  • Set clear ownership and operating cadences across the team so each workstream (tech and data, donor experience, knowledge management) has a defined remit and reduces duplicated effort across Fundraising verticals.

Act as the go-to liaison between Fundraising and other functions

  • Maintain a comprehensive view of Fundraising needs across all verticals and sub-teams, and act as the single point of contact for Grants Management, Finance, and Compliance on run-rate donor management processes.
  • Represent Fundraising's operational needs to the People team, Legal, and other functions as cross-functional systems and initiatives are designed and launched.

Partner with the VP on strategy and organizational effectiveness (chief-of-staff functions)

  • Collaborate with the Vice President to refine the unit's strategy, manage organizational change, and lead internal communications.
  • Streamline decision-making, manage priorities, and provide strategic counsel to maximize the VP's focus and effectiveness on high-impact work.
  • Prepare briefing materials and executive-level communications for senior leadership and Board audiences as needed.

Lead on cross-fundraising initiatives and priorities

  • Address broader organizational priorities as needed, including high-level donor stewardship coordination, cross-functional system launches, flexible workforce planning, or market expansion initiatives.

This role would suit somebody who is comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, who is energized by building systems and structure out of ambiguity, and who enjoys pulling together disparate workstreams into a cohesive, impactful strategy. It's a strong fit for someone with a business operations, revenue operations, or chief-of-staff background who wants a role weighted toward building and owning systems (and, over time, building a team) rather than one focused primarily on executive support.

What we're looking for

  • 8+ years of experience in revenue operations, business operations, or a chief-of-staff role, ideally within a fundraising, sales, or partnerships organization.
  • Demonstrated experience building or owning CRM/pipeline systems (e.g. Salesforce), KPI frameworks, and reporting infrastructure that multiple teams rely on.
  • Strong analytical operator: comfortable structuring ambiguity, setting priorities, and using data to drive decisions. An advanced degree (e.g. MBA) is a plus, not a requirement.
  • Proven track record managing cross-functional relationships and influencing senior stakeholders outside a direct reporting line.
  • Experience managing people or workstreams, with the ability to scope roles and structure as a function grows; direct people management experience is a plus given this role may build and lead a team of 3-5.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, particularly for high-stakes internal and Board-facing materials.
  • Deep alignment with GiveDirectly's values, especially recipient choice, transparency, and evidence.

Bonus

  • Experience working with institutional donors or fundraising teams in Africa.
  • Experience standing up a BizOps or RevOps function from scratch, including building out a team across tech and data, donor experience, and knowledge management.

Compensation

At GiveDirectly, we strive to pay our employees generously and equitably. We use an accredited third party salary aggregator to calculate what we believe to be competitive pay based on role, location, and cost of living. We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

Unless otherwise noted, the benefits stipend may be used to cover benefits or taken as additional taxable income.

For Director level:

United States

  • Base Salary: $134,400

Thumbtack helps millions of people confidently care for their homes.

Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. We help homeowners know which projects to do, when to do them and who to hire from our growing community of 300,000 local service businesses. If making an impact inspires you, join us. Imagine what we’ll build together.

About the Pro Activation & Success Team

Thumbtack's Pro Activation & Success pillar helps local service businesses discover Thumbtack, get started, find success, and grow with us over time. We build products and experiences that help more pros thrive, partnering closely with marketing, partnerships, and sales across the full pro journey. We're a highly collaborative, data-driven team united by a simple goal: helping pros build stronger businesses.

About the role

Thumbtack was originally built to serve individual professionals and small businesses. Now, larger and more sophisticated businesses represent one of our biggest opportunities for growth — and serving them well requires us to rethink what Thumbtack can offer. In this role, you'll shape how we win with this segment, from connecting Thumbtack with the tools pros use to run their businesses to creating the foundational experiences they need to succeed at scale. You'll work closely with our partnerships and business development teams to turn integrations into meaningful growth, identify and scale new growth levers tailored to this segment, and bring differentiated products to market.

What you’ll do

  • Own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for unlocking growth among larger, more sophisticated pros, with accountability for customer and business outcomes.

  • Develop a deep understanding of how these pros operate, using research and data to identify unmet needs, product gaps, and new opportunities for growth.

  • Set the strategy for our APIs, data integrations, and partner offerings, working directly with partnerships, business development, and external partners to create value for pros and open new growth channels.

  • Lead new products and capabilities from early discovery through launch and adoption, helping complex businesses succeed on a product originally designed for smaller businesses.

  • Partner with engineering to make thoughtful tradeoffs between near-term opportunities and durable technical foundations that can support future products and partnerships.

About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is looking for a strategic, execution-oriented Director of Internal AI Operations to run and continuously improve how our company adopts and scales AI, establish the operational objectives, processes, and work plans that turn AI from a collection of tools into a measurable business capability and work with leaders across several functions to put the company’s AI direction into practice.

Responsibilities:

  • Reporting: Build and maintain visibility into AI spend and usage. Develop adoption, efficiency, and cost metrics and report on tool overlap, cost drivers, and open risks. Support Finance with forecasting, budget tracking, anomaly detection, and vendor and model-cost optimization. Functional and technical leaders own efficiency, waste, cost, usage, and ROI within their portfolios; AI Operations prepares regular reporting and flags performance gaps for follow-up.
  • Portfolio management: Maintain the inventory of AI tools, initiatives, agents, vendors, integrations, owners, status, spend, risks, and dependencies. Establish the processes and standards that keep it accurate across teams.
  • Reviews: Participate in reviewing new AI Vendor requests and own and manage the Internal AI Feature Review process from intake through decision, conditions, approval, exception, or rejection, coordinating inputs from Security, Legal, IT, and business owners.
  • Policy operations: Develop and maintain the company’s Internal AI Policy supporting resources with Legal and Security, and the Executive team, along with supporting resources. Recommend policy changes and put approved changes into operation.
  • Transformation and migration: Track the AI roadmap, migrations, platform dependencies, adoption milestones, resourcing, risks, and executive decisions.
  • Partnership with our technology teams: Collaborate on new AI product initiatives, empowering our product teams with how they identify and deliver value around AI.
  • Administration and audit: Define and audit standards for access, ownership, configuration, data controls, logging, retention, vendor settings, and offboarding.
  • Communications and enablement: Own the Internal AI communications calendar, stakeholder updates, FAQs, launch materials, training coordination, and policy-change communications.
  • CoE coordination: Establish a common cadence and minimum artifacts across distributed AI CoEs without centralizing their technical or domain ownership.

Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of progressively responsible experience in AI or technology operations, enterprise systems, data and analytics, FinOps, governance, transformation, or a related field, including 5+ years leading teams or complex cross-functional programs.
  • Demonstrated success designing, implementing, or scaling an operating model across multiple functions, including clear ownership, policies, processes, metrics, governance, and measurable outcomes.
  • Experience managing an enterprise portfolio of AI or technology tools, vendors, integrations, or platforms, including lifecycle management, access and administration, risk and controls, contracts, usage, and spend.
  • Strong financial, analytical, and data-driven mindset, with experience using tools such as Snowflake, Excel, Python, or equivalent; able to define adoption, efficiency, unit economics, ROI, and business-value metrics and turn complex data into executive-ready recommendations.
  • Strong financial and operational acumen, with experience building spend visibility, forecasts, budget controls, vendor or model-cost optimization, cost avoidance, waste reduction, and value-improvement plans.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex topics clearly, present recommendations to senior and executive leaders, and persuade diverse stakeholders.
  • Experience influencing functional and technical leaders without relying on direct authority, clarifying distributed accountability, benchmarking performance, challenging tradeoffs, and driving follow-through across global, remote, and cross-functional teams.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to lean into AI: able to learn emerging capabilities quickly, experiment pragmatically, identify high-value use cases, and apply sound judgment about where AI should and should not be used.
  • Practical understanding of responsible AI, data governance, privacy, security, vendor risk, and change management, with the judgment to balance innovation, control, scalability, and business value.
  • Strong systems thinking, program management, prioritization, and change leadership skills; comfortable bringing structure to ambiguous, company-wide problems.
  • Experience hiring, coaching, or developing effective teams and building trusted partnerships across Finance, IT, Security, Legal, Procurement, and business functions.

What Success Looks Like:

  • Accelerate teams’ work through measurable improvements in cycle time, throughput, or capacity unlocked by AI.
  • Partner with functional leaders to demonstrate business value from priority AI use cases—not just increased usage.
  • Reduce friction from idea to responsible launch, measured by faster reviews, clearer decisions, and fewer stalled initiatives.
  • Improve AI portfolio efficiency through stronger utilization, reduced duplication, and better cost per user or workflow.
  • Establish trusted, scalable governance, with clear ownership, timely reviews, and consistent execution of required controls.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About The Role

We're looking for Product Managers across Senior, Staff, Principal, and Senior Principal levels who are curious builders, eager to drive company level impact and to build in an environment where AI is a core part of the toolkit.

We are hiring across Patient, Provider, Payer, and Platform. The right candidates will bring strong product fundamentals and a willingness to build with AI in a regulated, high-stakes industry. Product Managers at Headway own product areas end-to-end: setting strategy, partnering deeply with engineering, data science, and design, and driving outcomes that move the company.

The way we are building is continuously evolving, and the size of opportunity for Headway to leverage AI is massive. We sit at the intersection of healthcare delivery, complex insurance systems, and a multi-sided marketplace serving tens of thousands of providers and millions of patients.

The Problems We're Solving

For Patients

  • Finding the right therapist, understanding your insurance benefits, and staying in care shouldn't be hard. Today it is. We're building AI-powered matching and personalized care navigation that help patients get into — and stay in — mental health care at scale. One million patients a month ask for a referral to a mental health provider. We're building the systems that ensure they actually get there.

For Providers

  • Therapists spend a staggering amount of time on administrative tasks — credentialing, documentation, scheduling, billing — instead of with their patients. We're using AI to automate clinical workflows, simplify complex insurance requirements, and give providers more time to do what they came here to do. The goal: a thriving practice on Headway that practically runs itself.

For Payers

  • Health insurers are asking harder questions: Is care on Headway actually working? Is it worth what we're paying? We're using AI to answer them at scale — measuring clinical outcomes, building dashboards that demonstrate responsible care, and moving toward a model where patients are matched to the right care pathways and providers are aligned around better outcomes. This work protects Headway's standing with insurers and opens doors to deeper, more strategic partnerships.

For Platform

  • The infrastructure underneath Headway — billing, claims, payments, and trust and safety — needs to scale reliably at the speed of our growth. We’re using AI to automate complex, high-volume workflows, detect fraud and errors faster, and build systems that get smarter over time. This is foundational infrastructure with direct impact on Headway's economics and compliance posture.

What You'll Do at Headway

  • Define and own the product strategy for your area in partnership with engineering, design, data, clinical, and operations teams

  • Apply AI where it matters: identify where intelligence creates step-change improvements in your product area and drive those bets from insight through production

  • Set and own clear success metrics; communicate results and course-correct with urgency

  • Represent the voice of your customer — patient, provider, or health plan — with conviction in every decision, grounded in data and direct research

You'd Be a Great Fit If…

  • You have 8+ years of product management experience with a track record of owning complex, high-impact product areas

  • You have experience with LLM systems — prompting, retrieval, evaluation, fine-tuning — and a track record of shipping AI-powered products that hold up at scale, not demos.

  • You've built at scale in a marketplace, platform, or data-intensive environment — and can show the outcomes you drove

  • You're energized by working in regulated, complex industries and see constraints as a product design challenge rather than a blocker

  • You can influence across engineering, clinical, legal, finance, and operations — and you're equally comfortable in the data and in the room

  • You have strong quantitative fluency and can partner with data scientists on experiment design and causal analysis

  • You communicate with precision — in writing, in product reviews, and with senior leadership

CrossFit is seeking a Senior Product Manager, Education. You will own product strategy and execution for CrossFit's Education line of business, including the learner experience, course registration, content authoring and delivery, learning platforms, and credentialing. This is a hands-on, individual contributor role: you are the dedicated product specialist for Education, translating the needs of Education leaders, program owners, instructors, and learners into a clear product vision, roadmap, and priorities.

You will partner closely with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Operations, and Education leadership, and coordinate with product owners for adjacent products (for example, the mobile app) to align strategy and sequencing across the broader product surface. Education is central to CrossFit's identity and has significant room to grow. The foundation is an older, layered stack of in-house software and vendor tools.

This role requires someone resilient and responsive, strong at strategy, and disciplined about tight feedback loops: a person who can bring structure and clarity to ambiguity, make disciplined trade-offs, and deliver measurable results.

Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy & Roadmap:
    • Define and own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for Education, in alignment with company priorities and business objectives.
    • Establish clear product goals, success metrics, and KPIs, and regularly evaluate performance against expected outcomes.
    • Use customer insights, product analytics, market trends, and business data to identify opportunities and guide product decisions.
    • Balance learner experience, business impact, technical investment, and available resources, and make and communicate clear trade-off decisions when priorities compete.
    • Bring an informed point of view on where online learning is heading, then commit fully to the direction the business chooses.
  • Product Execution:
    • Lead the product lifecycle from discovery and validation through development, launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration.
    • Guide product decisions for Education's learner experience, course registration, content authoring and delivery, learning platforms, and credentialing, including integrations across existing systems.
    • Evaluate build, buy, modernize, or replace options for legacy platforms and vendor tools, considering user needs, technical dependencies, migration costs, and long-term value.
    • Ensure requirements clearly define the customer problem, business need, expected outcome, and measures of success.
    • Partner with Engineering and Design to scope initiatives and sequence work across quick wins, foundational fixes, and new capabilities.
    • Support launches with go-to-market, communication, training, and adoption plans in partnership with business stakeholders.
    • Contribute to foundational platform capabilities that cut across products, such as data privacy and consent, localization, and marketing enablement.
  • Customer & Business Impact:
    • Partner with Education leaders and program owners to identify learner and instructor pain points, distinguish underlying problems from proposed solutions, and prioritize improvements across the learner journey.
    • Establish and improve instrumentation for enrollment, course completion, conversion, learner retention, and revenue per learner, including where existing data is incomplete.
    • Run experiments across acquisition, activation, upgrades, and re-engagement, using results to refine product and growth priorities.
    • Build tight feedback loops through research, analytics, and direct engagement with learners, instructors, and staff, and turn what you learn into decisions quickly.
    • Tie product investments to measurable customer and business outcomes rather than feature delivery alone.
  • Collaboration & Influence:
    • Serve as the key Product partner to Education leadership, and communicate strategy, roadmap decisions, progress, risks, and results to executives and other stakeholders.
    • Establish operating rhythms that create visibility into roadmap progress, dependencies, risks, and decisions.
    • Identify and resolve barriers to execution across teams and functions.
    • Model strong product practices, including discovery, prioritization, and measurement, and share them with peers.
    • Coordinate with product owners for adjacent products to align strategy and sequencing.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Strong product judgment, with the ability to connect customer needs, business strategy, technology, and financial outcomes.
  • Knowledge of education technology, including learning management systems, content authoring, course delivery, credentialing, and learner-facing experiences, and/or deep experience in growth: funnel analysis, experimentation, activation, conversion, and retention. Depth in both is ideal.
  • Ability to define meaningful funnel and learning metrics, improve measurement capabilities, and use experimentation to inform product decisions.
  • Experience navigating legacy systems, vendor integrations, and fragmented data environments, with sound judgment on technical and migration trade-offs.
  • Strong strategic thinking, paired with resilience and responsiveness. You turn feedback into decisions quickly and stay steady when plans change.
  • Ability to prioritize investments and make difficult trade-offs in a resource-constrained environment.
  • Skill at finding the real problem behind a stated request, and at saying no in a way that keeps the relationship intact.
  • Strong understanding of modern software development and experience partnering closely with Engineering and Design.
  • Uses modern AI tools (e.g., Claude) fluently to accelerate discovery, requirements, analysis, and delivery.
  • Experience with lifecycle marketing and personalization tooling preferred.
  • Excellent communication and executive presentation skills, with demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and create alignment across functions.
  • Comfortable operating in an evolving environment, bringing structure and clarity to ambiguity.
  • Strong ownership, accountability, and bias toward execution.
  • Understanding of the CrossFit ecosystem, Affiliate model, or fitness industry preferred.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • 7+ years of product management experience for Senior, or 10+ years for Principal, including significant ownership of digital products or platforms.
  • Experience with education technology, certification or credentialing, online learning, or learner growth products, and/or growth product experience across acquisition, activation, conversion, and retention.
  • Familiarity with learning standards (such as SCORM or xAPI), international localization, registration and payment flows, or membership-based education models preferred.
  • Demonstrated success launching and improving products that delivered measurable customer and business outcomes, ideally in an older or complex technology environment.
  • Experience partnering closely with Engineering, Design, and senior business leaders.
  • Experience with consumer, B2B, marketplace, membership, subscription, fitness, or community-based digital products preferred.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you will lead the teams responsible for supporting, expanding, and strengthening the global affiliate network. You will define the strategic vision, drive key performance metrics, and collaborate across all HQ departments to deliver practical, high-impact solutions for affiliate owners.

As someone who has operated an affiliate, managed operations, coached athletes, and driven business growth, you will leverage your firsthand operational experience to support thousands of affiliate owners in scaling sustainable, successful businesses.

Key Outcomes

  • Network Growth & Retention: Drive affiliate network expansion while enhancing retention strategies and tracking core performance metrics.
  • Affiliate Advocacy & Support: Provide robust operational support, foster direct feedback channels, and serve as the primary advocate for affiliate owners within HQ.
  • Operational Excellence: Streamline business operations, establish clear performance benchmarks, oversee budget allocation, and leverage data-driven insights.
  • Team Leadership: Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team focused on execution, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Business Model Optimization: Enhance unit economics for affiliates and ensure all HQ initiatives deliver tangible value to local gym owners.

Key Responsibilities

  • Strategic Execution: Lead overall strategy and execution for the affiliate business unit, maintaining accountability for quarterly performance targets.
  • Community Engagement: Engage directly with affiliate owners through site visits, community events, and roundtables to gather field intelligence and align HQ priorities.
  • Unit Economics: Analyze affiliate unit economics to identify drivers of sustainability, growth, and operational risk across the network.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner cross-functionally with Education, Sport, Marketing, Product & Technology, Finance, and Legal to ensure cross-departmental alignment.
  • Budget Management: Manage the departmental operating budget in collaboration with Finance, optimizing resource allocation to yield high impact for owners.
  • Operational Improvement: Monitor key performance indicators, streamline workflows, and remove operational friction for local gym operations.
  • Team Mentorship: Coach, mentor, and cultivate leadership development within the affiliate operations team.

Qualifications & Core Competencies

  • Affiliate Ownership: Current ownership and operational experience with a CrossFit affiliate.
  • Certifications & Open Participation: Active CrossFit Level 4 (CF-L4) certification and ongoing active participation in the CrossFit Open.
  • Strategic Analysis: Strong analytical and strategic planning skills with a focus on measurable outcomes.
  • Affiliate-First Leadership: Agile, affiliate-first leadership style with a dedication to eliminating low-value processes.
  • Team Building: Proven capability to build trust, inspire teams, and develop talent effectively.

Education & Experience

  • Executive Leadership: 10+ years of progressive executive leadership in business operations, account management, franchise/network operations, or professional services.
  • Remote Team Management: Demonstrated expertise managing senior leaders and leading geographically dispersed or remote organizations.
